 42 weather alerts in effect 19 homes evacuated as Oak Creek floods parts of Sedona 
 There are three to four inches of water inside the homes, officials say 
 At least 19 homes have been evacuated along Oak Creek as firefighters called in extra crews Sunday morning to conduct an “excessive amount” of water rescues. By Brian Petersheim Jr. and Haley Williams Published : Nov. 1, 2026 at 8:20 AM MST | Updated : 7 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google SEDONA, AZ (AZFamily) — At least 19 homes have been evacuated along Oak Creek as firefighters called in extra crews Sunday morning to conduct an “excessive amount” of water rescues as floodwaters rose rapidly.
 Homes in the area have flooded with three to four inches of water, according to David S. McAtee, Yavapai County’s Communications Manager and Public Information Officer.
 RELATED: Active flooding evacuations across Arizona: Here’s who’s impacted 
 According to the Sedona Fire District , evacuations primarily impact neighborhoods on the city’s east side within Zones 8, 9, and 10. 
 Sedona Fire and Sedona Police are “evaluating multiple folks trapped in their residences due to rising water,” Sedona Fire District Chief Ed Mezulis told the local newspaper, Sedona Red Rock News.
 The Yavapai County Sheriff’s Office reported deputies helped with evacuations near Red Rock Crossing in Sedona. Crews are also helping with evacuations along Oak Creek and off Rimrock Drive, as well as conducting a rescue operation on Perkinsville Road.
 Officials urge anyone in immediate danger to move to higher ground immediately and call 911 when safe.
 RELATED: Interstate 17 reopens after flooding forces closure; some Arizona highways stay closed 
 Officials say an evacuation shelter has been established at Sedona Red Rock High School . 
 Authorities remind residents to avoid washes and creek beds, and warn drivers to never attempt crossing flooded roadways.
 Your zone can be found by clicking here . 
 Tlaquepaque closure
 Tlaquepaque is closed Sunday due to the flooding. Their Day of the Dead celebration has also been canceled. 
 “DO NOT attempt to visit Tlaquepaque, it is not safe,” village officials said. 
 This is a developing story. Check back for updates.
